# US2014 (rebuilt from public BTS data following Barkol et al.'s documented procedure; passenger itineraries generated by us)

**This is not the original US-2014 dataset.** Barkol et al. (HP Labs, 2016) built US2014 for ROADEF-2009-style recovery, but
their scenario files sit in a private Dropbox and the wiki ([github.com/tomersagi/us2014](https://github.com/tomersagi/us2014))
delegates the hard parts to HP-internal Java/Talend tools that are not public (`PlanSimulator`, `MaintenanceFileGen`,
`DisruptionsSimulator`, `AirportCapacitySimulator`, `ItineraryGenerator`, `AutomatedPassengerAllocator`, `ItineraryFixer`,
"Prepare Supporting Data"). We re-implemented the documented procedure from the public sources and wrote our own
substitutes for those tools. The numbers will differ from the HP report; every substitute is listed below.

The result is a set of ROADEF-2009-format instances (`config.csv`, `aircraft.csv`, `flights.csv`, `rotations.csv`, ...)
that `arp.instance.load_instance` reads unchanged.

## Reproduce

```bash
cd arp_rh
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt           # pandas, pyarrow, tzdata, httpx are needed for the builder
python -m arp.us2014.download                       # public inputs (about 1.1 GB), checked against us2014/raw_manifest.json
python -m arp.us2014.build --instance US03 US08_EMB120 US02_CRJ700 US08_CRJ700 US02_A320 US08_A320 US02_B737 US02_CRJ200 US02_A320_NQ US02 US04 US05 US06 US07 US08 US09 US10
python -m arp.us2014.build --verify                 # instance files vs us2014/instances/CHECKSUMS.json
python -m arp.us2014.build --check-determinism      # rebuild US03 twice, compare hashes
python -m arp.us2014.download --check               # raw files vs us2014/raw_manifest.json (no network)
```

Building with `--instance` keeps `CHECKSUMS.json` as published, so `--verify` compares the rebuild with the instances of
the paper. `--all` rebuilds the 16 benchmark instances, then rewrites `CHECKSUMS.json`, `validation.json` and the tables
below and runs the full-horizon gate (10 min per scale-down instance). Raw files and `us2014/cache/` are reused if present,
so a warm rebuild takes about 35 s (a cold one adds the download and about 1.5 min of parsing). Everything is seeded
(`--seed 1`; per-instance seed = crc32(name) xor seed), and rebuilding gives byte-identical files.
Use an instance from the solver: `from arp.instance import load; I = load("US02_CRJ700", "../roadef2009")` (names are
registered in `INSTANCE_DIRS`).

**What is distributed.** The public release contains the builder, this documentation, `raw_manifest.json`, `models.csv`,
the instance checksums, build statistics and validation report, but not the instance files themselves: they are rebuilt
from the sources below. The three files taken from the upstream repository (which has no licence) are not redistributed
either; `download.py` fetches them from github.com/tomersagi/us2014 at commit `4802d7f` and checks their SHA-256.

## Sources (retrieved 2026-10-04, all pinned in `raw_manifest.json`)

| input | source | use |
|---|---|---|
| On-Time Performance 2014, 12 monthly files (about 280 MB) | `transtats.bts.gov/PREZIP/On_Time_Reporting_Carrier_On_Time_Performance_1987_present_2014_{1..12}.zip` | flights, delays, cancellations, tails |
| DB1B Coupon 2014 Q1-Q4 (about 800 MB) | `.../Origin_and_Destination_Survey_DB1BCoupon_2014_{1..4}.zip` | route demand |
| T-100 Segment (All Carriers) 2014, all 12 months | BTS field-selection form `DL_SelectFields.aspx?gnoyr_VQ=FMG`, replayed by `download.py` (437,082 rows; class F, UA/EV/OO used) | load factors, demand scaling |
| `combinedPlaneData.csv`, `airportCoordinates.csv`, F41 inventory zip | upstream repo `data/sources/` at commit `4802d7f`, fetched into `us2014/upstream_sources/` | fleet with F/C/W/Y configs, airport time zones |

The numbered PREZIP T-100 snapshots (`896816367_T_T100*`) are unusable (May 2014 only, or no passengers/seats); the real
full-year 2014 table came from the form replay. If that route breaks, drop the CSV at `us2014/raw/T100_SEGMENT_2014.csv`; if it
is absent the build falls back to the DB1B x10 sample rate (monthly = quarterly x 10/3), which is also the wiki's default factor.

## Instances

| name | what | capacity basis |
|---|---|---|
| `US02`, `US04`...`US10` | wiki scenarios 2, 4-10: whole United network, 3 days (recovery start 14:00 GMT day 1, end 23:59 day 3) | network (wiki) |
| `US03` | wiki scenario 3: the EMB-120 Brasilia tails of scenario 2 | network (wiki) |
| `US02_CRJ700`, `US02_A320`, `US02_B737`, `US02_CRJ200` | scale-down sub-fleets on the scenario-2 dates (OO CRJ-700, UA A320 family, UA B737 family, OO CRJ-200) | own flights |
| `US08_EMB120`, `US08_CRJ700`, `US08_A320` | the same idea on the scenario-8 dates (August) | own flights |

Scale-down rationale: the whole-network scenarios have 9,200-11,400 flights (3-4x the 2,844 rotation entries of B01), far beyond the exact full-horizon (FH)
MIP. Aircraft only swap within a *family* (here an aircraft type family, e.g. `CRJ700`, `A320`, `B737`), so sub-fleets are separable
by construction. The family of seven scale-down instances has 684-2,160 flights. Sub-fleet quotas are computed from the
instance's own flights (a network-wide quota would be slack for a single fleet); `US03` keeps the wiki's network quotas.
`US02_A320_NQ` is a sensitivity twin of `US02_A320` (not one of the 16 benchmark instances; skipped by `build --all`, built with `--instance US02_A320_NQ`): identical flights, tails, itineraries and random streams, but the wiki's network-basis quotas and reductions instead of quotas from the sub-fleet's own flights. It tests how much of the rolling-horizon gap comes from our quota substitute.
The checksums of all instance files are in `instances/CHECKSUMS.json`.

## Faithful steps and substitutes

| wiki component | what we did | status |
|---|---|---|
| airports, time zones | OTP origin/destination joined to `airportCoordinates.csv`; local `CRSDepTime` converted to UTC with the IANA zone (pandas/zoneinfo); arrival = departure + `CRSElapsedTime` | faithful, Python tz database instead of `tzdata.*` tables |
| SampleFlights | OTP rows with reporting airline in UA/EV/OO and tail in `combinedPlaneData` (N27523 -> N13979) | **count not reproduced** (see below) |
| scenarios 2-10 | wiki dates; flights with departure in the window and arrival <= scenario end | faithful. Scenarios 4 and 6 are labelled "Full 4 days" in the wiki but span 3 days; dates kept |
| scenario 3 | EMB-120ER tails of scenario 2 (40 of the 62 are active in the window) | faithful |
| plane models (Talend, private) | `models.csv`, generated by `make_models.py`: range = 1.1 x longest scheduled block time of the model in 2014 OTP; turn/transit = 2nd percentile of scheduled ground times clamped to [20, 30/40/60 by size class]; operating cost per hour linear in seats, fitted by eye to the ROADEF 2009 aircraft table (not a Form 41 figure); family = aircraft type family | **substitute** |
| cabins | F = first, B = business (`C` in the config string), E = premium economy + economy (`W` + `Y`); 2 tails without a config string are excluded | premium economy merged (ROADEF has 3 cabins) |
| start/end positions | start = origin of the tail's first flight in the window; `position.csv` = last arrival airport counted by (model, config) | faithful |
| rotation repair (`PlanSimulator`, private) | per tail, longest chain with continuity, no overlap, turnaround >= model turn (exact DP, ties towards flights that actually flew); dropped flights are removed. Rerun on the output drops 0 (the wiki's "0 invalid sub-rotations") | **substitute**, drop rate in the table |
| cancellations before the recovery start | removed from the instance (history; they would break the executed chain of fixed flights) | our choice |
| maintenance (`MaintenanceFileGen`, private) | each tail gets one 4-6 h block with probability 0.15, in a ground gap >= 8 h after the recovery start; `Remaining` = minutes from scenario start to maintenance start (the wiki's `DATEDIFF`) | **substitute** (ROADEF A/B have about 3-16 % of aircraft with maintenance) |
| airport capacity | hourly (GMT) max over the scenario days of max(planned, actual) departures/arrivals; actual = planned if `ArrDelayMinutes` <= 15, else shifted; hours with no observed movement have capacity 0 (as in the wiki's COALESCE) | faithful to the SQL views |
| flight disruptions | wiki SQL: cancellations that are not carrier-caused and delays > 15 min, kept if cancelled, departing before the recovery start, or externally caused; delay = `ArrDelayMinutes`, cancel = -1 | faithful |
| fixed-flight delays | delays of fixed flights are propagated down each tail's fixed chain so that the executed history respects turnaround (the wiki uses the arrival delay as the departure delay, which can break it) | our fix, counted in `build_stats.json` |
| aircraft disruptions (`AircraftDisruptions`, private) | carrier-caused cancellations (code A, which the wiki excludes from flight disruptions) of flights departing after the recovery start are read as outages: tail unavailable from the cancelled departure to its next planned departure | **substitute, inferred**. UA mainline cancellations carry no tail number in OTP, so UA tails get no outages |
| airport disruptions (`AirportReduction`, private) | in hours after the recovery start where network planned minus actual movements >= max(3, 30 % of planned): rate = actual (network basis) or proportional (fleet basis) | **substitute** |
| capacity fix (`AirportCapacitySimulator`, private) | reduced rates are raised to the number of immovable (fixed, possibly delayed) movements in that hour; rerun reports 0 updates (the wiki's check) | **substitute**, same stopping criterion |
| penalties | ROADEF 2009 values (27 delay/cancel rows, 9 downgrade rows), P1/P2/P3 = 20000/5000/1000, alpha = beta = gamma = 1 | the wiki's 18 downgrade rows include 9 premium-economy rows that ROADEF cannot express; the wiki's scenario-1 values are in the private DB, so we assume the ROADEF ones |
| flight type | wiki rule: `C` if both airports are in the same country; OTP is US-domestic, so every flight is `C` (`--type-rule distance` gives D/C/I by distance) | faithful, hence the type-dependent penalties are one column |
| route / `dist.csv` | mean planned block minutes per directed pair that is flown | faithful |
| itineraries | see below | **substitute** |

### Itinerary generator (replaces ItineraryGenerator, AutomatedPassengerAllocator, ItineraryFixer)
* Demand: DB1B coupons with operating carrier UA/EV/OO. Non-stop trip = a coupon between two trip breaks; one-stop trip = two
  consecutive coupons with no break between them (maximum 2 flights). Differences from the wiki SQL: non-stop demand counts trips, not
  all coupons (otherwise connecting passengers are counted twice).
* Scaling: monthly demand = DB1B quarterly passengers x clip(T-100 monthly / DB1B quarterly, 2, 5), minimum over the two legs, default
  3.33 (the wiki's rule), spread evenly over the days of the month (no weekday factor).
* Candidates: non-stop flights and 2-leg pairs with 30 <= connection <= 180 min, a carrier pair seen in DB1B, at most 6 per route and day.
* Allocation: multinomial logit (elapsed time, connection penalty, night departure); the original `choiceparams.properties` is not public,
  so the parameters are our assumptions. Then iterative proportional fitting so that flight loads match T-100 load factor x seats (cap 95 %);
  seeded integer rounding; premium cabins open only where every leg has seats; no cabin is ever overbooked (seat spill is 0 in the baseline).
* Price: Y = 100 + total miles / 5 (the wiki: first leg only), cabin multipliers B 1.5, F 2 (premium economy merged, so no 1.25). All itineraries have type `A`.
* Checks (as in the wiki): 0 itineraries with a connection < 30 min or a mismatched connection airport, none with more than 2 flights.
* In sub-fleet instances only connections within the sub-fleet exist (2-leg pax share is 2 % for CRJ-700 against 15 % for the whole network).

## Comparison with the wiki

* **Full-year SampleFlights = 1,164,155 is not reproduced.** Our base filter (UA/EV/OO and tail in `combinedPlaneData`) gives 1,441,228
  (+23.8 %). The closest simple filters are in the table below (UA+EV, any tail: 1,179,546, +1.3 %). OTP has no codeshare/marketing
  carrier column, so "United-branded" EV/OO flights cannot be separated from their Delta/American flights; the wiki's exact filter is unknown.
  The wiki's second check (458,582 `tempTZ` rows) is an odd intermediate and is not attempted.
* Penalty rows 27 (reproduced) and 18 (we have 9, see above); "0 invalid sub-rotations" is reproduced by the repair rerun.
* The HP report's per-scenario statistics are not available to us (ResearchGate returns 403), so instance sizes could not be compared.

## Solver gate (part of `build --all`)

Every instance with <= 2,500 flights (US03 and the seven sub-fleets) is solved with the exact FH model (HiGHS, LP-restricted,
10 min limit, one solver process at a time) on the *disrupted* instance and must give `n_violations == 0`; obj, bound, gap, status and
runtime are in `instances/validation.json` and in the FH-gate table above. The full-network scenarios (9k+ flights) only get the
undisrupted-twin check.

**Root cause found by an earlier gate run (`US02_CRJ700`, tail `CRJ700#66`).** The generator placed a maintenance block at MKE
(start minute 1710) on a tail whose fixed flight had a 390 min historical delay. Sub-fleet airport quotas come from the instance's own
flights, and hours without observed movement have rate 0: MKE had exactly one arrival slot (hour 1620-1680) in the whole day, and
reaching it after the delay needed an arrival at minute 1681, one minute late. The FH model therefore paid the 1e5 maintenance-location
slack. No evaluator/model mismatch: the instance itself had no feasible plan. **Fix (generator):** maintenance is only placed on tails
whose rotation up to the maintenance gap is untouched by the generated disruptions (no delayed/cancelled flight, fixed or not; no
outage; no departure or arrival in an hour with a reduced airport rate). Maintenance is therefore drawn after disruptions and airport
reductions.

**Gate classes.** An instance whose solver plan has `n_violations == 0` is `solver-feasible`. If the solver plan has violations, the
instance passes only as `hard (witness-feasible)`: `instances/<name>/witness_plan.json` (compact JSON, flight `number|date` -> `null` or
`[dep, arr, tail]`) is re-evaluated by `evaluate()` at build time and must give `n_violations == 0` (the stored number is never trusted;
the witness survives rebuilds and is covered by `CHECKSUMS.json`). `pos_missing` of the witness is recorded but not required: end-of-recovery
positions are soft in ROADEF, and a historical cancellation can make a shortfall unavoidable (the best witness found has 28). Otherwise `FAIL`
and `build --all` exits non-zero. `build --all --reuse-gate` reuses stored solver results for unchanged instances and only redoes the witness check.

**`US02_B737` (1,529 flights): fails the 10-min fine-grid gate, but is solvable.** The gate run (fine grid, 10 min, default LP method) does not converge: after 10 min, and again after 15 min warm-started from the rule-based OCC plan, the incumbent is the OCC-quality plan (obj 43.50 M, bound 14.6 M, gap 66 %) with one `maint_location` violation (tail `B737-800#32`, maintenance at DEN from minute 1510). The instance is not defective: an explicit plan with `n_violations == 0` exists (stored as `witness_plan.json`, total 43,189,569), and, more to the point, the **coarse delay grid with the interior-point LP method (`--lpm ipm`, 1,200 s limit) solves it in 199 s to a 0.16 % gap with 0 violations** (total 15,293,300; `arp_rh/results_us2014/US02_B737__fh-coarse.json`). The gate therefore labels it `hard (witness-feasible)` only because the gate uses the fine grid and a 10-min limit; for experiments it is a regular, FH-solvable instance on the coarse grid. The gate record is kept unchanged (it is regenerated by `build --all`).

## Rotation repair and itineraries

Itineraries are generated *after* the repair, from the retained flights only, so dropped flights never appear in `itineraries.csv`
(their demand is not re-assigned, so the pax total is lower by about the drop rate). The validation checks this directly: the column
"itineraries referencing dropped flights" counts itinerary legs missing from `rotations.csv`, and is 0 for every instance. The drop rate
per instance is the last column of the summary table (4.5-12 %; cancellations before the recovery start are removed first and not counted).

## Known issues and open questions

1. **Rotation-repair drop rate is 4.5-12 %** (above the 5 % at which ferry flights should be considered). The drops come from
   discontinuities in OTP tail records (in a diagnostic on US02 before the pre-start cancellations were removed, 44 % of the discontinuities involved cancelled flights, which keep their scheduled tail; positioning flights are not in OTP) and from tail
   swaps. Inserting ferry flights instead of dropping is the obvious next step.
2. The wiki's SampleFlights filter and count are not reproduced (above).
3. Maintenance, aircraft outages, airport reductions, plane-model parameters and the choice model are substitutes; none can be checked against HP data.
   Ask the author whether HP's report tables are available, and for the HP `PlaneModel` values.
4. `US02_B737` fails the 10-min fine-grid FH gate (label `hard (witness-feasible)`), but the coarse grid with the IPM LP method solves it in 199 s at 0.16 % gap with 0 violations (see the paragraph above); the fine-grid FH remains unsolved in 10-15 min.
5. Maintenance now avoids disrupted tails (see the solver gate); a consequence is that fewer tails carry maintenance than before.
6. Revelation times are not produced (ROADEF has none); `arp/scenarios.py` can add them.
7. Citation/permission note for the rebuilt dataset: the HP paper is cited as the source of the procedure; the data are public BTS data.

## Files

`arp_rh/arp/us2014/`: `download.py`, `build_base.py` (OTP, DB1B, T-100), `make_models.py`, `scenarios.py` (windows, repair,
maintenance, capacity, disruptions), `itineraries.py`, `export_roadef.py`, `build.py` (CLI), `validate.py`, `summary.py`.
`us2014/`: `models.csv` (generated, committed), `raw_manifest.json`, `instances/<name>/` (ROADEF files + `tails.csv` id -> N-number + `build_stats.json`),
`instances/CHECKSUMS.json`, `instances/SUMMARY.md`, `instances/validation.json`.
